lens_verdicts.summary: The S5 windowed probe chain is genuinely well built where it was rewritten: `FrameTimeRing.record()` is allocation-free BY CONSTRUCTION (fixed `LongArray` + Int arithmetic, no boxing), the overflow fact travels with the drained data instead of as a flag, both S5 actuals carry a generation guard, and both `rememberWindowedTemporalProbe()` implementations dispose the self-reposting loop on composition exit. Six concerns survive falsification. The one that is NOT latent: the Paso-5 observer-effect fixes (B1 bounded buffer, B2 no boxing, B3 dispose) were applied to `WindowedTemporalProbe.android.kt` but NOT to its sibling `FrameTimingProbe.android.kt`, which is the one with a live production call site (`SpeedExerciseScreen.kt:112`) — it still holds an unbounded boxing `ArrayList<Long>`, still self-reposts, and has no `DisposableEffect`, so an abandoned Velocidad run leaks a per-vsync callback whose own GC churn is then classified by the very same probe as the user's jank (B5, live). Second: the iOS actual still computes `droppedFrames`/`criticalFrameJitter` against a cadence derived from the same trace — the exact self-referential method the same file's comment declares forbidden — and emits them; only the separate `expectedCadenceHz = null` field keeps the policy from consuming them. Third, and the reason the first one survived: every observer-effect and performance-budget claim in this chain (dispose is "load-bearing", 8 KiB budget, "allocation-free", "no boxing per frame") is asserted only in a KDoc — no type and no test goes red if any of them is deleted, even though this same test suite already has the source-guard idiom (`WindowedTemporalProbeCadenceHonestyTest`, `Focus2PlatformPermissionTest`) that would catch them. For focus2 itself blast radius is zero: `rememberWindowedTemporalProbe()` has zero call sites repo-wide.

The per-WINDOW layer is honest and well-tested: `TemporalClassPolicy.windowIntegrity` refuses to classify without both an expected and a delivered cadence, maps buffer overflow to `NoObservation` (never `Excluded`), and fails closed on NaN/zero/negative reference rates. I could not falsify any of those. The failure is that `NoObservation` — produced correctly — protects nothing downstream. `FocusTemporalEligibility.evaluate` counts NO_OBSERVATION cells as `windowsClassified` and excludes only the EXCLUDED bucket from the fraction, and its `NotCaptured` guard fires only on EMPTY cells. A session whose windows are 100% unclassifiable therefore yields coverageComplete=true, excludedFraction=0.0 and verdict **Eligible**. That is not a corner case: iOS declares `expectedCadenceHz = null` unconditionally, so EVERY iOS window is `NoObservation` and every iOS session lands on that path — reported as `T1_FRAME_OBSERVED` ("frame cadence observed by an authoritative monotonic probe") because the session frame floor is fed by `sampledFrames` from windows whose cadence was never resolved. Total absence of temporal observation is rendered as a full pass, in the flattering direction the charter names as the more dangerous inversion. No test covers it: the eligibility oracle's entire input domain is {Clean, Excluded, null} — `NoObservation` and `DegradedUsable` are never fed to `evaluate()`, so its "reachable codomain fully exercised" claim pins the outputs while omitting half the inputs. Secondary: iOS still computes drop/jitter against the SELF-DETECTED cadence with a fabricated 60 Hz fallback — the exact self-reference its own comment says the charter forbids (inert today only because `expectedCadenceHz=null` forces NoObservation, but recorded as fact on the observation); Android reports a fabricated `droppedFrames = 0` when the platform stated no cadence, which makes `frameDropFraction()` return 0.0 against a KDoc promising "never a fabricated 0.0"; the two actuals recover the drop count asymmetrically (`roundToInt` vs truncating `toInt`); and `FrameTimingProbe.android.kt` — in this manifest and, unlike focus2, PRODUCTION-WIRED via SpeedExerciseScreen — still substitutes 60 Hz for an unreadable display rate, the very defect the sibling adapter was just fixed for. Blast radius of every focus2 finding today is ZERO (the engine is unmounted, zero production call-sites); F6 is the one exception, in the Speed lane.

The arithmetic does NOT support the verdict. The load-bearing defect is that `windowsClassified` is a misnomer: it counts every trial FOLDED into a temporal cell, including windows whose verdict was `NoObservation` — the typed statement "this window produced no classifiable observation". `TemporalClassPolicy` is honest here (a window with no expected cadence is `NoObservation`, "not a clean window, it is no window"), but `FocusTemporalEligibility.evaluate` then scores that same window as classified (numerator denominator), covered (`coverageComplete`), and non-excluded (contributes 0 to the numerator). A session in which NOT ONE window was ever classifiable therefore evaluates to `sessionClass = T1_FRAME_OBSERVED`, `coverageComplete = true`, `excludedFraction = 0.0`, `rtShadowVerdict = Eligible` — absence fabricating perfection, the exact inversion the charter names as the more dangerous one. On iOS this is not an edge case: `expectedCadenceHz` is unconditionally `null`, so EVERY window is `NoObservation` and EVERY iOS session lands on that path; the iOS adapter's own comment claims "Declared absent ⇒ NotCaptured", which the arithmetic contradicts (`NotCaptured` fires only on EMPTY cells, and a `NoObservation` verdict is non-null so it populates cells). No test in the tree drives `NoObservation` through `evaluate`; the "adversarial oracle" that claims a generated domain sweep is built from a two-element verdict alphabet `{Clean, Excluded(TRUNCATION_RISK)}` plus null, so it is structurally incapable of catching this. Secondary: the only sample floor in the whole path is a FRAME count (120), never a TRIAL count, so a 2-trial session is Eligible (the oracle's own honest half pins this at n=2); and `excludedFraction == null` fails CLOSED in `evaluate` (→1.0) but OPEN in `FocusEvidenceStatePolicy.evidenceOf` (→0.0) for the same underivable quantity. On the items I was asked to check and found CLEAN: there is no double counting between the excluded-resolved numerator and the discard denominator (resolved-excluded trials are read from `cell.totalTrials`, discards from `excludedByReason`, and a discard leaves `cell.totalTrials == 0`); the ceiling comparison direction is strict `>` consistently with every KDoc; the config validator's refusal to order `windowDropExcludeMin` against `sessionExcludedMax` is correct — those ARE different populations, and the two orderings it does assert are same-unit; and the 0.50 backstop is reachable in both directions (0.4286 passes, 0.60 trips), so it is not decorative. Blast radius today is ZERO: focus2 is deliberately unmounted, `evaluate` has no production call-site, and no official verdict is altered. Every finding is latent, rated by what it does WHEN WIRED.

VERIFIED CLEAN (4 of the 5 charge items): (1) only SUMMARIES are persisted — the two serialized types are `FocusSessionDescriptor` (sealed constants) and `FocusRuntimeSnapshot`, which holds `List<ConditionTally>`/`List<TemporalCellTally>` integer SDT counts and per-reason exclusion counts, with no per-trial list, no latency and no ordered series; every checkpoint overwrites the SAME key so no history accumulates on disk. (2) No device fingerprint is persisted: refresh rate crosses into a serialized type only BANDED (`HzBand`, ±5% buckets, `FocusSessionDescriptor.nominalHzBandName`); the raw `view.display.refreshRate` lives only in the ephemeral, non-`@Serializable` `TemporalWindowObservation`; no model, OEM, build or absolute timestamp anywhere. (3) No PII and no raw `Throwable` reaches any sink — `FocusWriteOutcome.Failed(error::class.simpleName)` carries the type name only, and a grep of the whole focus2 + core.timing tree finds ZERO logging/Crashlytics/Observability call-sites (no sink exists at all). (4) Account ERASURE of `mindboost_focus2` is mechanically enforced, not assumed: the namespace is in `AccountBound`, wired into `SecureNamespaceUserDataEraser` in the same AppGraph list, resolved through `accountBoundEraserStores` which fails fast on an unwired namespace, and pinned by `AccountBoundErasureCoverageTest`. WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY CLEAN: the fifth item — REVOCATION. Unlike its two sibling stores, focus2 has no `SubjectRevocationAuthority` guard anywhere, so a write landing after erasure resurrects rows that `restore()`/`scanSessionIds()` will read back (F1). Plus a reachable residual-retention hole (F2: a failed seal + process death orphans a snapshot the drain can never enumerate), an in-memory ordered per-trial behavioural series with zero readers that falsifies the engine's own "holds COUNTS, never trials" claim (F3), and a permission guard whose scan scope excludes the only source sets where a permission could appear (F4). Blast radius of ALL findings today is ZERO: focus2 is deliberately unmounted, nothing constructs `FocusTracerStateHolder` or `SecureFocusSessionStore` in production, and the namespace is empty. Severities are rated for what each would do WHEN WIRED.

This is the one finding whose blast radius is NOT zero: that probe is wired into the Speed lane.
3. **The drain still precedes the rejection check** (FocusTracerStateHolder.kt:205 vs 210) — the removal comment 130 lines above diagnoses that ordering as the root cause of the bug it removed, then leaves the ordering in place.

Plus four documentation/duplication observations. Blast radius today is zero for everything in focus2; F1 and F2 must be closed before the wiring step, and F2 warrants a look at the Speed lane independently of this phase.

lens_verdicts.lens: L7-tests (vacuity / claim-vs-assertion audit of the S5 test suite)
lens_verdicts.summary: The suite is far better than average: the d′ goldens are genuinely independent (I recomputed 1.310847 / 1.680016 / 1.292908 / 1.329617 by hand from the log-linear H/FA rates and they match), most rejection tests carry a real discriminating half, the adversarial oracle declares cardinalities instead of `> 0`, and the checker-sensitivity sentinel proves the monotonicity checker has teeth. But ten tests prove less than their names/KDocs claim. The most serious is a hole in the suite's flagship claim: the "0/0 trap" is pinned ONLY for the empty-cells absence. A session whose windows all resolve to `NoObservation` — the honest "we could not measure this" verdict, and the ONLY verdict iOS can produce in S5 since `expectedCadenceHz = null` always — folds into non-empty NO_OBSERVATION cells, so `evaluate()` returns `windowsClassified = n`, `coverageComplete = true`, `excludedFraction = 0.0` and **`Verdict.Eligible`**. That is absence fabricating perfection at session level, in the exact direction the charter calls the more dangerous one, and no test in the manifest ever feeds a NoObservation window into `evaluate()`. Everything is latent: focus2 is unmounted, blast radius today is zero. F-01 should be closed before any wiring decision; the rest are pin-tightening.

refutations.reasoning: The claim's arithmetic is accurate but its consequence does not exist. iOS hardcodes `expectedCadenceHz = null` unconditionally at WindowedTemporalProbe.ios.kt:88, one line below the code the claimant quoted. TemporalClassPolicy.kt:53-55 routes any observation failing `cadenceResolved` to NoObservation BEFORE any threshold runs, and `cadenceResolved` (:75-77) requires `expected != null && detected != null`. Therefore every iOS window is NoObservation, and the self-detected `droppedFrames`/`criticalFrameJitter` are only ever read inside `conservativeVerdict` (:89-96) — the else-branch iOS can never reach. Repo-wide grep confirms `droppedFrames` has exactly two readers: `frameDropFraction()` (TemporalWindowObservation.kt:49) whose sole caller is `dropFractionOf` in that unreachable branch. The DEFAULT_REFRESH_HZ fallback is doubly dead: the frozen-timestamp case the claimant constructs (FrameStatsCalculator.kt:81 returns null when median <= 0) also sets `detectedCadenceHz = null` at ios.kt:89, so cadenceResolved fails on both operands — the fabricated-perfect window is discarded, never blessed as Clean. FocusTracerStateHolder.kt:203-207 forwards only the verdict and sampledFrames into runtime.respond (FocusSessionRuntime.kt:100-105); the observation is never persisted or read elsewhere. Finally, the comment the claimant cites as self-contradiction (ios.kt:85-87) is written in the past tense about a defect that was removed ("what this adapter used to do implicitly") and :88 is the fix; the honesty test cited as blessing the fallback (WindowedTemporalProbeCadenceHonestyTest.kt:53-54) explains this exact shape distinction and its neighbouring test pins `expectedCadenceHz = null, detectedCadenceHz = 60.0 -> NoObservation`. Residue worth noting but not a defect: the values are still computed as dead quantities on the observation, and the class KDoc at ios.kt:26-28 is stale (describes self-detection in the present tense as design rationale) relative to :85-88 — a hygiene/doc risk on a latent path, not an honesty violation. Blast radius today is zero either way: focus2 is unmounted.

REFUTED. The claimant's factual observation is literally true (an Android window with no stated cadence carries sampledFrames>0 and droppedFrames=0, so frameDropFraction() evaluates to 0.0), but the inference "nothing catches it" is wrong, and the guard they dismiss as unrelated is the guard designed for exactly this condition.

1) Single call-site, and it is guarded on the causing field. `frameDropFraction()` is read in exactly one place in all of shared/src: TemporalClassPolicy.kt:100 `checkNotNull(observation.frameDropFraction()) { "sample gate must run before thresholds" }`, inside `private fun dropFractionOf`, reachable only from `private fun conservativeVerdict`, reachable only from the `else` branch of `windowIntegrity` (TemporalClassPolicy.kt:49-56). That branch is entered only after `!cadenceResolved(observation, thresholds)` (:53) failed to fire, and `cadenceResolved` requires `expected != null` (:77). The elvis default on the Android side fires ONLY when `expectedHz == null` (WindowedTemporalProbe.android.kt:80 `val stats = expectedHz?.let { FrameStatsCalculator.fromFrameTimes(times, it) }`). Same field, same predicate: the 0.0 is unreachable by construction, not by luck.

2) "Shielded only incidentally, by an unrelated guard at :53" is false. The guard lives in the SAME `when` guard clause as the sample gate, and its KDoc is written about precisely this case — TemporalClassPolicy.kt:63-64 "A 'dropped frame' is defined relative to an expected period, so with no stated expectation there is nothing to drop from (iOS in S5)". The Android adapter's comment is the mirror of it — WindowedTemporalProbe.android.kt:76-77 "With no stated rate there is no definition of 'dropped', so no drop count is computed at all — reporting zero drops against an absent reference is how absence fabricates a flawless window." Both sides name the same rule; the claimant treats a two-sided design as a coincidence.

3) The exact flagged shape is pinned by a test that fails if the policy is weakened. WindowedTemporalProbeCadenceHonestyTest.kt:69-81 constructs `TemporalWindowObservation(sampledFrames = 60, droppedFrames = 0, criticalFrameJitter = false, expectedCadenceHz = null, detectedCadenceHz = 60.0)` — i.e. verbatim the Android null-cadence output — and asserts `TemporalWindowVerdict.NoObservation`, with the class KDoc at :20-21 stating the test exists so "weakening the policy turns this red too rather than leaving a guard that protects nothing." So the shape is deliberate, documented, and regression-locked.

4) No other escape route for the field. grep over shared/src for `droppedFrames` returns only: the data-class declaration (TemporalWindowObservation.kt:12), the accessor (:49), and the two adapter constructors (android :86, ios :79). Nothing else reads it. The runtime receives only the verdict and the frame count — FocusTracerStateHolder.kt:206-211 `val verdict = observation?.let { TemporalClassPolicy.windowIntegrity(it, temporalThresholds) }` / `val sampled = observation?.sampledFrames ?: 0` / `runtime.respond(response, atElapsedNanos, verdict, sampled)`. The fabricated 0.0 has no consumer even hypothetically-when-wired.

5) The KDoc "promise" is over-read. TemporalWindowObservation.kt:47 reads "Drop fraction, or `null` when nothing was sampled (never a fabricated 0.0)". The null is explicitly conditioned on "nothing was sampled"; the parenthetical explains why 0/0 is not rendered as 0.0. It does not promise null for "drops were not computed", so the accessor does not contradict its own contract.

Residual, and why it is not a defect: `droppedFrames: Int` cannot represent "unknown", so an unknown is typed as zero on a public data class — the only genuine kernel here, and it is a deliberate trade documented at WindowedTemporalProbe.android.kt:82-83 ("Same unit either way: `sampledFrames` counts INTER-FRAME DELTAS, so the session floor accumulates the same quantity whether or not the window was classifiable"). Zeroing sampledFrames to force the accessor to null would silently shrink the session frame floor that TemporalClassPolicy.sessionClass (:25 `sampledFramesSession >= thresholds.minFramesSession`) consumes — a real regression traded for a hazard with no reachable consumer.

Severity: the claim is P2 on a defect that cannot fire. Blast radius today is zero (focus2 is unmounted, zero production call-sites) AND zero when wired, because the sole wiring path (FocusTracerStateHolder.submit -> windowIntegrity) is the guarded one. Not a defect; at most a P3-flavoured note about the field's type, already argued for in the source.

Every factual assertion in the claim is verbatim-verifiable, so it cannot be refuted. (a) The substitution exists: FrameTimingProbe.android.kt:55-56 `val hz = view.display?.refreshRate?.toDouble() ?: FrameStatsCalculator.DEFAULT_REFRESH_HZ` / `if (hz > 0.0) hz else FrameStatsCalculator.DEFAULT_REFRESH_HZ`, with the KDoc at :47-48 admitting "Falls back to the conservative 60 Hz nominal when the view is not yet attached or the platform reports a non-positive rate." (b) The type at :19 `private val refreshHzProvider: () -> Double,` cannot express absence, unlike the sibling at WindowedTemporalProbe.android.kt:34 `private val refreshHzProvider: () -> Double?,` and :120-122 "No fallback constant: a detached view (or a nonsense rate) means the platform stated nothing". (c) The guard's scope genuinely excludes this file — WindowedTemporalProbeCadenceHonestyTest.kt:95-97 binds ANDROID_ADAPTER only to WindowedTemporalProbe.android.kt. (d) It is production-wired and load-bearing: SpeedExerciseScreen.kt:112/:142 -> SpeedSessionStateHolder.kt:109, :325 `val frameStats = frameProbe.stop()`, :331-332 into QualitySignals -> SessionQualityEvaluator.kt:83-90 (CONTAMINATED) -> SpeedProfileSource.kt:100 excludes CONTAMINATED/LOW from the profile; seven live screens (E1DestelloScreen.kt:21 .. E7CompuertaScreen.kt:21) route through it, so blast radius is not zero here.

Severity is nevertheless overstated, on two independent grounds the claimant did not read.

1. The proposed fix is behaviorally inert, contradicting the claim's core assertion that "the fabrication is not an oversight that can be patched at the call site". Retyping the provider to `() -> Double?` still leaves the adapter able to return only FrameStats, and FrameStatsCalculator.kt:41-43 maps an absent/non-finite rate to FrameStats.UNAVAILABLE, defined at FrameTimingProbe.kt:19-24 as `frameDropFraction = 0.0, criticalFrameJitter = false`. Those two fields are the ONLY frame signals reaching the gate (SessionQualityEvaluator.kt:83 `if (signals.criticalFrameJitter)`, :87 `if (signals.frameDropFraction > thresholds.contaminatedFrameDropThreshold)`); `sampledFrames` is never placed into QualitySignals. So the "honest" null path yields the same no-jank verdict, and today's 60 Hz constant is equal-or-stricter (a >25 ms stall still counts as a drop, where UNAVAILABLE counts nothing). The fabrication of perfection would move, not disappear.

2. The real fabricated-perfection defect is one layer down and is not this file: FrameStats.UNAVAILABLE encodes "not measured" as zero drops, and is returned unconditionally on every non-Android target (FrameTimingProbe.kt:39-42, FrameTimingProbe.desktop.kt:7, FrameTimingProbe.ios.kt:10) — orders of magnitude more reachable than this file's trigger. That trigger is narrow: `Display.getRefreshRate()` is a non-null Float, so the elvis at :55 fires only when `view.display` is null (detached view), while stop() is invoked from assembleRun() during live composition. The high-refresh-panel masking the file's own KDoc :13-16 describes is already fixed on the normal path.

The asymmetry with the sibling is also principled rather than an oversight: there, null propagates into a genuine absence verdict (TemporalWindowObservation.expectedCadenceHz = null -> TemporalClassPolicy.windowIntegrity -> NoObservation, pinned at WindowedTemporalProbeCadenceHonestyTest.kt:67-82); FrameStats has no absence-aware verdict to propagate into, so the rule cannot buy honesty here without first fixing FrameStats/QualitySignals.

Real, worth a ticket as a structural-honesty wart on a live lane, but P3: the named fix changes no verdict, and the deeper "unknown == clean" fabrication belongs to FrameStats.UNAVAILABLE / QualitySignals, not to line 55.

Refutation attempt FAILED — the defect is real as described, verified against the pinned manifest bytes (sha256 of FocusTemporalEligibility.kt = 25d1e6fa…, WindowedTemporalProbe.ios.kt = cb509dda…, TemporalClassPolicy.kt = 1ae8b44d…, FocusSessionReducer.kt = d242694f…, all matching C4_REVIEW_TARGET_MANIFEST.txt).

CHAIN CONFIRMED BYTE BY BYTE:

FocusTemporalEligibility.kt:78 `val windowsClassified = cells.sumOf { it.cell.totalTrials }`; only :79-81 filters, and only for EXCLUDED (`.filter { it.bucket == TemporalWindowBucket.EXCLUDED }`). :91 `if (denominator > 0) (excludedResolved + discards).toDouble() / denominator else null` ⇒ all-NoObservation gives 0/N = 0.0, not null.
(2) NoObservation really folds a counted cell. FocusSessionReducer.kt:197-199 `temporalCells = temporalVerdict?.let { snapshot.temporalTallying(conditionId, it, outcome) } ?: snapshot.temporalCells` — the elvis skips only a NULL verdict; NoObservation is a non-null data object (TemporalWindowVerdict.kt:33). FocusRuntimeModel.kt:161 `TemporalCellTally(conditionId.name, key, (existing?.cell ?: SdtCell.EMPTY) + outcome, counted)` increments totalTrials (DescriptiveModel.kt:140/143).
(3) coverageComplete cannot catch it — structurally impossible. :92 `windowsClassified == snapshot.resolvedTrials`; both sides are incremented by the SAME outcome in the same reduction (reducer :191 official tally, :197 shadow cell), so an all-NoObservation session is "fully covered".
(4) sessionClass cannot catch it. TemporalClassPolicy.kt:23-29 uses only capability/clock-domain agreement plus `sampledFramesSession >= thresholds.minFramesSession` (=120, TemporalQualityThresholds.kt:83). On iOS every drain contributes (WindowedTemporalProbe.ios.kt:78 `sampledFrames = stats.sampledFrames,`) while :88 guarantees the window is unclassifiable, so `minFramesSession = 120` (TemporalQualityThresholds.kt:83) is cleared in ~2 s of frames.
findings.when_wired: The sealed session descriptor and any downstream consumer read T1_FRAME_OBSERVED — the engine's own label for 'we measured the cadence' — on sessions where the cadence was never resolved once. Combined with the finding above, iOS produces (T1_FRAME_OBSERVED, Eligible) from total temporal absence. A buffer-overflow storm on Android has the same shape: those windows are NoObservation by design (FrameTimeRing.kt:16-20) yet their frames still count toward claiming authority. Blast radius today is ZERO (unmounted).

findings.title: iOS classifies the frame stream against itself and falls back to a fabricated 60 Hz — the self-reference its own comment forbids
findings.claim: `droppedFrames` and `criticalFrameJitter` are computed with the SELF-DETECTED median cadence as the reference period, and with the fabricated `DEFAULT_REFRESH_HZ` constant when the median is underivable. Classifying a trace against a statistic of that same trace is auto-consistent by construction: any steady cadence, however degraded, yields ~0 drops. The file's own comment 12 lines below states this is the false negative the charter forbids, and the class KDoc at :26-28 presents it as a deliberate design choice.
findings.evidence: WindowedTemporalProbe.ios.kt:75-76 `val detectedHz = FrameStatsCalculator.detectedRefreshHz(times)` / `val stats = FrameStatsCalculator.fromFrameTimes(times, detectedHz ?: FrameStatsCalculator.DEFAULT_REFRESH_HZ)`, feeding :79 `droppedFrames = (stats.frameDropFraction * stats.sampledFrames).toInt(),` and :80 `criticalFrameJitter = stats.criticalFrameJitter,`. Contradicted in the same file at :85-87: `// Self-detecting the rate and classifying against it — what this adapter used to do implicitly — makes a half-rate window read as flawless, which is the false negative the charter forbids.` The reference it uses is derived from the judged data: FrameStatsCalculator.kt:76-82 `fun detectedRefreshHz(frameTimesNanos: LongArray): Double? { ... val median = deltas[deltas.size / 2] ... }`. The constant fallback is reachable with >=2 frames whenever the median delta is non-positive (duplicate/frozen timestamps): FrameStatsCalculator.kt:81 `return if (median > 0L) NANOS_PER_SECOND / median else null` — a frozen CADisplayLink then yields all-zero deltas judged against a 16.67 ms period, i.e. 0 drops, criticalFrameJitter=false: absence fabricating a flawless window. The honesty test explicitly blesses this: WindowedTemporalProbeCadenceHonestyTest.kt:53-54 `iOS DOES use the nominal constant to compute descriptive stats`.
findings.when_wired: Inert for the verdict today because :88 `expectedCadenceHz = null` forces NoObservation — but these are recorded on the public observation as facts, and the ADR anticipates a session-trend consumer for exactly this series. The first consumer that reads `droppedFrames`/`criticalFrameJitter` from an iOS observation inherits numbers that can only ever say 'clean'. The honest form is Android's: compute nothing when there is no defensible reference (android.kt:80 `val stats = expectedHz?.let { ... }`). Blast radius today is ZERO (unmounted).

findings.title: Android reports droppedFrames = 0 for a window where drops were never computed, so frameDropFraction() returns a fabricated 0.0
findings.claim: When the platform states no cadence, the adapter correctly declines to compute stats — then writes `droppedFrames = 0` alongside a positive `sampledFrames`. `TemporalWindowObservation.frameDropFraction()` returns null only when `sampledFrames == 0`, so it returns 0.0 for this window, directly against its KDoc promise 'never a fabricated 0.0'. The unknown is typed as zero on the public data type; `TemporalClassPolicy` happens to be protected by a different guard, so nothing catches it.
findings.evidence: WindowedTemporalProbe.android.kt:84-86 `sampledFrames = stats?.sampledFrames ?: (times.size - 1).coerceAtLeast(0),` / `droppedFrames = stats?.let { (it.frameDropFraction * it.sampledFrames).roundToInt() } ?: 0,` — sampledFrames > 0 with droppedFrames elvis-defaulted to 0. Blast radius today is ZERO (unmounted).

findings.title: FrameTimingProbe.android still substitutes 60 Hz for an unreadable display rate — and this path IS production-wired

Its provider is typed `() -> Double`, so it structurally cannot express 'the platform stated nothing' — the fabrication is not an oversight that can be patched at the call site. Unlike everything else in this review, it has live production call-sites.
findings.evidence: FrameTimingProbe.android.kt:54-57 `AndroidFrameTimingProbe {` / `val hz = view.display?.refreshRate?.toDouble() ?: FrameStatsCalculator.DEFAULT_REFRESH_HZ` / `if (hz > 0.0) hz else FrameStatsCalculator.DEFAULT_REFRESH_HZ` / `}`, with the non-nullable contract at :19 `private val refreshHzProvider: () -> Double,`. On a 90/120 Hz panel a null `view.display` (detached view during a lifecycle transition) yields a 16.67 ms nominal instead of the true 8.33 ms one, so genuine jank pacing at 60 Hz reads as flawless against the fabricated reference — the file's own KDoc at :13-16 describes this exact failure as the reason the hardcode was removed, while leaving the fallback that reintroduces it. Blast radius here is NOT zero, though the window is narrow (the view is normally attached mid-exercise).

findings.title: The two actuals recover the drop count asymmetrically; iOS truncates, biasing only toward fewer drops
findings.claim: Both adapters recover an integer drop count by multiplying a fraction back by the sample size, but Android rounds and iOS truncates. `toInt()` truncates toward zero, so floating-point recovery of e.g. 2.9999999 reports 2. The error is one-directional — it can only under-report drops — so the same physical frame stream is graded more leniently on iOS than on Android.
findings.evidence: WindowedTemporalProbe.ios.kt:79 `droppedFrames = (stats.frameDropFraction * stats.sampledFrames).toInt(),` versus WindowedTemporalProbe.android.kt:86 `droppedFrames = stats?.let { (it.frameDropFraction * it.sampledFrames).roundToInt() } ?: 0,`. The quantity being recovered is itself a division: FrameStatsCalculator.kt:61 `frameDropFraction = drops.toDouble() / deltas,` — so `fraction * deltas` is not exact for most drop/delta pairs.
findings.when_wired: Cross-platform comparability of the drop fraction is broken in the flattering direction on iOS. Currently masked because iOS windows are all NoObservation (see the iOS self-reference finding), so the count is never consumed by a verdict. Blast radius today is ZERO (unmounted).

findings.title: FrameStatsCalculator keeps a default refreshHz that silently supplies an unmeasured 60 Hz, and the fail-closed guard cannot catch it
findings.claim: Both overloads default the reference cadence to a constant. The guard added right below rejects NaN, zero, negative and infinite — every way of expressing 'no answer' EXCEPT the one the default itself supplies, because 60.0 is finite and positive. A caller that omits the argument gets a full classification against a cadence nobody measured, and no guard anywhere can tell that apart from a measured 60 Hz panel.
findings.evidence: FrameStatsCalculator.kt:26 `fun fromFrameTimes(frameTimesNanos: List<Long>, refreshHz: Double = DEFAULT_REFRESH_HZ): FrameStats =` and :36 `fun fromFrameTimes(frameTimesNanos: LongArray, refreshHz: Double = DEFAULT_REFRESH_HZ): FrameStats {`, with the guard at :41 `if (frameTimesNanos.size < MIN_FRAMES || !refreshHz.isFinite() || refreshHz <= 0.0) {` — whose own comment at :37-40 frames the problem correctly ("an ABSENT input fabricating a flawless stream — the exact inversion the charter forbids") but leaves the default as the one absent input that passes. Constant at :13 `const val DEFAULT_REFRESH_HZ: Double = 60.0`. Mitigating: every production call site currently passes explicitly — android.kt:80, FrameTimingProbe.android.kt:41, ios.kt:76 — so only tests exercise the default today (e.g. FrameStatsCalculatorTest.kt:22 `val stats = FrameStatsCalculator.fromFrameTimes(frames)`).
findings.when_wired: A latent trap rather than a live defect: it is the same 'absence dressed as a statement' that was just removed from the Android adapter, still available one layer down to the next caller who omits the argument. Making the parameter required (or nullable with a null result) would close the family at its root instead of adapter-by-adapter. Blast radius today is ZERO.

findings.title: `NoObservation` windows are scored as classified, covered and non-excluded — a session with zero classifiable windows evaluates to Eligible with excludedFraction 0.0 (absence fabricating perfection; the whole iOS platform sits on this path)
findings.claim: `windowsClassified` counts trials folded into ANY bucket, including NO_OBSERVATION — the bucket that means "no verdict was derivable". Because the numerator only ever grows from the EXCLUDED bucket and from discard reasons, a wall of NoObservation windows produces excludedFraction = 0/N = 0.0, coverageComplete = true, and (given an authoritative capability and >=120 frames) sessionClass = T1_FRAME_OBSERVED. All three exclusion causes stay empty, so the verdict is `Eligible`. The gate designed to detect unmeasurable capture returns its MAXIMUM score precisely when nothing was measured.
findings.evidence:
FocusTemporalEligibility.kt:78 `val windowsClassified = cells.sumOf { it.cell.totalTrials }` — no bucket filter. :79-81 `val excludedResolved = cells.filter { it.bucket == TemporalWindowBucket.EXCLUDED }.sumOf { it.cell.totalTrials }` — NO_OBSERVATION contributes nothing to the numerator. :91 `if (denominator > 0) (excludedResolved + discards).toDouble() / denominator else null`. :92 `val coverageComplete = windowsClassified == snapshot.resolvedTrials` — both sides count the same trials, so an all-NoObservation session is "fully covered". :105 `rtShadowVerdict = if (causes.isEmpty()) Verdict.Eligible else ...`.

The type's own contract says NoObservation must bite here — TemporalWindowVerdict.kt:26-28: "[DegradedUsable]/[NoObservation] keep behaviour attributable ... and only constrain shadow RT / coverage." `evaluate` constrains neither.

The adapter comment at ios:87 asserts "Declared absent ⇒ NotCaptured" — false: `NotCaptured` requires `cells.isEmpty()` (FocusTemporalEligibility.kt:63), and a NoObservation verdict is non-null so the reducer folds a cell (FocusSessionReducer.kt:197-199 `temporalCells = temporalVerdict?.let { snapshot.temporalTallying(conditionId, it, outcome) } ?: snapshot.temporalCells`).
No test catches it: `NoObservation` appears ZERO times in FocusTemporalEligibilityTest.kt, and the adversarial oracle's entire verdict alphabet is FocusTemporalEligibilityAdversarialOracleTest.kt:51-52 `private val excluded = TemporalWindowVerdict.Excluded(WindowExclusionReason.TRUNCATION_RISK)` / `private val clean = TemporalWindowVerdict.Clean` — two of four buckets, so the "codomain sweep" at :426-431 cannot reach this state.

The failure is silent and one-directional: it never rejects an honest session, it only admits unmeasured ones, so it will not surface as a bug report — it will surface as a shadow RT distribution nobody can defend. Blast radius TODAY is zero (focus2 unmounted, no call-site).

findings.title: The only sample floor in the temporal path is a FRAME count, never a TRIAL count — two trials satisfy "authoritative" and there is no n floor on eligibility at all
findings.claim: `minFramesSession = 120` is a count of inter-frame deltas, i.e. a property of the DISPLAY, and it is the sole quantity standing between a session and `T1_FRAME_OBSERVED`. At 60 Hz with the engine's own 1.2 s response window that is ~72 deltas per trial, so the floor is crossed at trial 2. Neither `evaluate` nor `rtShadowAdmissible` imposes any floor on `windowsClassified` (the psychometric unit), so a 2-trial session can be `Eligible` and RT-shadow-admissible. A frame count certifies that the panel refreshed; it certifies nothing about how many windows produced an agreeing cadence — which is why it composes so badly with the NO_OBSERVATION hole above.

TemporalQualityThresholds.kt:83 `private const val MIN_FRAMES_SESSION: Int = 120`, whose KDoc at :25-26 claims "Below this, the session cannot claim an authoritative cadence ⇒ T0". FocusTemporalEligibility.kt:56-107: `evaluate` contains no comparison against any minimum window/trial count; the three causes at :93-99 are class, coverage and the excluded ceiling only. FocusEvidenceStatePolicy.kt:55-57 `rtShadowAdmissible ... temporal?.rtShadowVerdict == FocusTemporalEligibility.Verdict.Eligible` — no n gate either.

findings.title: The same underivable `excludedFraction == null` fails CLOSED in `evaluate` (→1.0) and OPEN in `FocusEvidenceStatePolicy` (→0.0); the KDoc only justifies the other null
findings.claim: `evaluate` declares in a named constant that an underivable fraction "can never pass a below-ceiling check (fail-closed, not a fake 0.0)" and substitutes 1.0. The composing policy substitutes 0.0 for the identical value. The elvis `temporal?.excludedFraction ?: NO_BACKSTOP` collapses TWO distinct nulls: `temporal == null` (no evaluation ran — the case the KDoc defends, "NotCaptured must not demote accuracy evidence") and `temporal != null && temporal.excludedFraction == null` (an evaluation ran and the fraction is UNDERIVABLE). Only the first is justified; the second is an unjustified fail-open that contradicts `FULLY_EXCLUDED` by exactly 1.0, and it is the literal fabricated 0.0 the charter forbids. Two opposite defaults for one absent quantity is not a policy, it is a divergence waiting for the two files to be read separately.
findings.evidence:
FocusEvidenceStatePolicy.kt:45-46 `(temporal?.excludedFraction ?: NO_BACKSTOP) > thresholds.sessionExcludedMax -> FocusEvidenceState.TRAINING_ONLY` with :60 `private const val NO_BACKSTOP: Double = 0.0`. Directly against FocusTemporalEligibility.kt:96 `if ((excludedFraction ?: FULLY_EXCLUDED) > thresholds.sessionExcludedMax)` with :109-110 `/** An underivable fraction can never pass a "below ceiling" check (fail-closed, not a fake 0.0). */ private const val FULLY_EXCLUDED: Double = 1.0`. The justification at FocusEvidenceStatePolicy.kt:59 covers only the first null: "Absent temporal capture triggers no backstop: NotCaptured must not demote accuracy evidence." The property core takes the eligibility side, making the policy the odd one out — FocusTemporalEligibilityProperty.kt:72-73 `private fun exclusionRank(evaluation: TemporalEvaluation): Double = evaluation.excludedFraction ?: FAIL_CLOSED_MAX` and :94 `private const val FAIL_CLOSED_MAX: Double = 1.0`, whose comment at :60-62 says absence "orders ABOVE every derivable fraction ... matching the SUT's own `?: FULLY_EXCLUDED` guard".

Every reducer path forbids it — `temporalTallying` always adds an outcome and every `TrialOutcome` increments `totalTrials` (DescriptiveModel.kt:140 `val totalTrials: Int get() = signalTrials + noiseTrials + omissions + anticipations`, :143-150 every branch +1), and `temporalDiscardCounting` always records a reason. It opens on DESERIALIZATION: `TemporalCellTally` defaults both fields (FocusRuntimeModel.kt:77-79 `val cell: SdtCell = SdtCell.EMPTY,` / `val excludedByReason: Map<String, Int> = emptyMap(),`) and the schema is declared N-1 readable (:190-191).
findings.when_wired: An evaluated session whose fraction is underivable is demoted to TRAINING_ONLY by one authority and promoted to PROVISIONAL by the other. Whichever consumer lands first silently picks the semantics, and since `evidenceOf` is the one that names the evidence state a user sees, the fail-OPEN is the one that ships. Blast radius today is zero (nothing consumes either).

findings.title: `discardReasons` is a hand-maintained 2-of-3 STRING subset of a closed enum with no exhaustiveness guard, and the numerator can double-count a resolved window the reducer's public API accepts
findings.claim: The discard vocabulary is a second, unpinned copy of `WindowExclusionReason`, matched by `.name` string, so neither the compiler nor a `when` exhaustiveness check protects it. A discard emitted under any reason outside the pair vanishes from BOTH numerator and denominator — invisible loss, not conservative loss. Separately, the numerator's two terms are only disjoint because the policy happens to emit `Excluded(TRUNCATION_RISK)` and nothing else: `FocusRuntimeInput.Respond.temporalVerdict` is a public field accepting any verdict, and a resolved window carrying `Excluded(PAUSE_DISCARD)` would be counted once via `cell.totalTrials` and again via the reason map. Bounded (numerator can never exceed denominator, so the fraction stays <= 1.0 and errs conservative) but the invariant is accidental, not enforced — and this is the same defect family the project's own 2026-08-18 learning names: a gate whose vocabulary is a second copy without a parity pin.

FocusTemporalEligibility.kt:82-88 `val discardReasons = setOf(WindowExclusionReason.PAUSE_DISCARD.name, WindowExclusionReason.CLOCK_EPOCH.name,)` then `val discards = cells.sumOf { cell -> cell.excludedByReason.filterKeys { it in discardReasons }.values.sum() }` — 2 of the 3 entries in TemporalWindowVerdict.kt:14-23 (`PAUSE_DISCARD`, `CLOCK_EPOCH`, `TRUNCATION_RISK`). The single producer is TemporalClassPolicy.kt:90 `TemporalWindowVerdict.Excluded(WindowExclusionReason.TRUNCATION_RISK)`, but the reducer contract does not require it — FocusRuntimeModel.kt:249 `val temporalVerdict: TemporalWindowVerdict? = null,`.

findings.title: The session backstop is a ceiling, not a selector: at exactly 0.50 the session passes and ALL its windows are admitted, and `TemporalEvaluation` discards the per-bucket breakdown a consumer would need to stratify
findings.claim: The comparison is strict `>` against 0.50, so a session where half the windows carry TRUNCATION_RISK returns `Eligible` — and eligibility is all-or-nothing at the SESSION level, so the excluded windows' behaviour is admitted alongside the clean windows' rather than dropped. Psychometrically that is a mixture: the admitted distribution is contaminated by windows the policy itself judged possibly truncated, with no way to weight or partition them, because `TemporalEvaluation` exposes only the aggregate fraction and not the CLEAN/DEGRADED/EXCLUDED counts. The strictness direction is defensible and matches every KDoc; the missing stratification is the part that has no defence in the type.
findings.evidence: FocusTemporalEligibility.kt:96 `if ((excludedFraction ?: FULLY_EXCLUDED) > thresholds.sessionExcludedMax)` against TemporalQualityThresholds.kt:86 `private const val SESSION_EXCLUDED_MAX: Double = 0.50`, whose KDoc at :31 reads "global excluded fraction above this ⇒ TRAINING_ONLY" — so `>` is correct, and the 0.50 boundary is deliberately pinned as passing: FocusTemporalEligibilityAdversarialOracleTest.kt:179 `val atHalf = evalAt(listOf(clean, clean, excluded, excluded)) // 2/4 = 0.50 exactly`. The exported shape drops the breakdown — FocusTemporalEligibility.kt:47-54 `data class TemporalEvaluation(val sessionClass, val windowsClassified, val coverageComplete, val excludedFraction: Double?, val rtShadowVerdict)` — and the sole RT gate reads only the session verdict: FocusEvidenceStatePolicy.kt:55-57 `rtModalityAdmissible && inputPrecision == InputTimestampPrecision.NANOS_NATIVE && temporal?.rtShadowVerdict == FocusTemporalEligibility.Verdict.Eligible`. Mitigating: the cells remain the single authority (FocusTemporalEligibility.kt:46 "derived — never persisted (single authority = cells)"), so a future consumer could stratify from the snapshot rather than from this type.
findings.when_wired: An RT lane fed by `rtShadowAdmissible` ingests up to 50% truncation-risk windows per session with no marking, so the shadow RT variance is inflated by a mechanism the data cannot separate afterwards — the same reason Paso 6 reframed its target as dispersion. findings.title: focus2 has no revocation guard: a write racing account deletion resurrects an erased subject's rows, and restore()/scanSessionIds() read them back
findings.claim: `SecureFocusSessionStore` consults no revocation tombstone on any read or write, so erasure of `mindboost_focus2` is a one-shot wipe with no anti-resurrection barrier — exactly the gap `SubjectRevocationAuthority` was built to close for the two sibling subject-scoped stores. A grep of the entire focus2 tree (commonMain + tests) returns zero hits for `SubjectRevocation`; the only matches for "revocation" are consent-scope revocation, an unrelated concept.
findings.evidence: Constructor takes storage and nothing else — `class SecureFocusSessionStore(private val store: SecureKeyValueStore, private val versions: EngineVersions = EngineVersions.CURRENT)` (SecureFocusSessionStore.kt:33-36). Both read paths are unguarded: `suspend fun restore(userId: String, sessionId: String): RestoreOutcome { val descriptor = readOrNull(descriptorKey(userId, sessionId)); val snapshot = readOrNull(snapshotKey(userId, sessionId))` (:56-58) and `suspend fun scanSessionIds(userId: String): SessionScan = try { SessionScan.Scanned(store.keys(prefix(userId))` (:93-95). Both write paths likewise: `sealDescriptor` (:42-43) and `checkpoint` (:46-47) call `write(...)` with no state check. Contrast the sibling namespaces, where the eraser routes through subject-scoped stores that DO consult a tombstone: `SecureCognitiveSessionRunStore(runsStore, revStore, subject = userId).deleteAll()` and `SecureSessionRecordStore(sessionsStore, revStore, subject = userId).deleteAll()` (AccountDeletionCoordinator.kt:72 and :80), and the tombstone is deliberately excluded from erasure precisely so it can block post-erasure writers — "an ANTI-RESURRECTION marker that MUST SURVIVE account deletion: blanket-clearing it ... would let a stale in-flight writer resurrect a deleted subject's data after erasure reported complete" (MindBoostStorageNamespaces.kt:74-77). focus2 gets the blanket clear (AccountDeletionCoordinator.kt:67-69) and none of the protection.
findings.when_wired: `FocusTracerStateHolder.checkpoint()` writes on EVERY resolved trial (FocusTracerStateHolder.kt:210-211, :288-294) and `start()` writes the seal (:159). `AccountDeletionCoordinator.recoverPendingDeletion()` runs on app entry on its own coroutine and calls `eraseUserData` (AccountDeletionCoordinator.kt:178), and `deleteCurrentAccount()` likewise (:165). A session coroutine that survives backgrounding — the exact scenario the write-ahead design exists for — can therefore land a `put` after `clearNamespace()` has run, re-creating `focus2_session:<erasedUid>:<sid>:descriptor` and `:snapshot`. Nothing later removes them: the drain in `start()` only ever runs for that same userId, who no longer exists, and a second local account scans a different prefix. The rows are then readable in full by `restore(erasedUid, sid)`. Reporting, not fixing, per instruction. Today: zero blast radius — the namespace is empty and no production call-site constructs this store.

findings.title: A failed seal plus process death orphans an encrypted snapshot the recovery drain can never enumerate — the exact silent retention the drain's KDoc claims to prevent
findings.claim: `scanSessionIds` enumerates ONLY keys ending in `:descriptor`, but a session whose seal failed still writes `:snapshot` rows on every trial. If the process dies before `complete()`, the snapshot is on disk with no descriptor, is invisible to every future drain, and has no deletion path other than account deletion. The same orphan arises when `discard` removes the descriptor but the snapshot removal fails.
findings.evidence: The scan filters descriptors only: `store.keys(prefix(userId)).filter { it.endsWith(DESCRIPTOR_SUFFIX) }.map { it.removePrefix(prefix(userId)).removeSuffix(DESCRIPTOR_SUFFIX) }` (SecureFocusSessionStore.kt:95-97), and `start()` deletes only what that scan returned — `if (scan is SessionScan.Scanned) { scan.sessionIds.forEach { id -> store.discard(userId, id) } }` (FocusTracerStateHolder.kt:156-158). A failed seal does NOT stop the run: `writeAheadSealed = sealed is FocusWriteOutcome.Stored` (:160) and the session proceeds as `FocusStartOutcome.PracticeOnly(sealed.reason)` (:165), while `submit()` unconditionally calls `checkpoint()` (:211) which writes the snapshot key (SecureFocusSessionStore.kt:46-47). The discard ordering leaves the same residue: `val snapshot = remove(snapshotKey(...)); val descriptor = remove(descriptorKey(...)); if (snapshot is FocusWriteOutcome.Stored) descriptor else snapshot` (:82-84) — a snapshot-remove failure with a descriptor-remove success is reported honestly but leaves an unreachable orphan. This falsifies the drain's own stated purpose: "without it a session killed by the OS leaves its buffer encrypted on disk with nothing on the device that ever looks at it again, which is silent retention however good the intentions were" (FocusTracerStateHolder.kt:141-143).
findings.when_wired: Indefinite on-device retention of one session's condition-level SDT counts and temporal cells for any run that hit a storage fault at seal time and was then killed. Content is coarse (integer counts, no PII, no latency, encrypted at rest) and account deletion's blanket `clearNamespace()` still reaches it, which caps the harm — but between those two events there is no enumeration path, no purge and no user-visible control, and the reader is left believing the drain covers this. Today: zero blast radius (unmounted, namespace empty).

findings.title: FocusSessionRuntime keeps an unbounded ORDERED per-trial emission series with zero production readers — the same write-only-series pattern Paso 7 just deleted one file over
findings.claim: `recorded` accumulates every emission for the whole session in order, and because `RESPONSE_SUBMITTED` is emitted only when the participant actually answered, the list reconstructs an ordered per-trial answered/omitted series — a behavioural stream. It is never cleared, never gated by purpose, consent or dose cap, and no production code reads it. This is the in-memory reincarnation of the per-trial record `FocusRuntimeSnapshot`'s KDoc says the engine deliberately does not hold.
findings.evidence: `private val recorded = mutableListOf<FocusEmission>()` / `/** Every emission so far, in order. The caller journals these; the runtime only remembers them. */ val emissions: List<FocusEmission> get() = recorded.toList()` (FocusSessionRuntime.kt:76-79), appended on every accepted reduction: `recorded += reduction.emissions` (:130). The series is behavioural because submission is conditional: `emissions = buildList { if (answered) add(FocusEmission(CanonEvent.RESPONSE_SUBMITTED, snapshot.trialIndex)); add(FocusEmission(CanonEvent.TRIAL_RESOLVED, snapshot.trialIndex)) }` (FocusSessionReducer.kt:202-205). A repo-wide grep for readers of `.emissions` finds only `FocusSessionReducerTest` and `FocusEventCatalogTest` — zero production consumers, so it is write-only. It contradicts the engine's own invariant: "**It holds COUNTS, never trials.** ... An earlier draft of this type carried a `List<RecordedResponse>` ... every session — tutorials included — left a complete behavioural record ... the engine cannot persist what it does not hold" (FocusRuntimeModel.kt:88-98). It is also the identical shape to the series removed in this same phase: "`windowVerdicts`, an ordered in-memory list ... it was WRITE-ONLY for three phases — grep found one writer and zero readers — while its comment advertised a consumer that does not exist ... An ordered series comes back WITH the detector that needs it, and its test" (FocusTracerStateHolder.kt:75-83). `recorded` survived that sweep.
findings.when_wired: The KDoc's "The caller journals these" points a future writer straight at a journal — the one surface `FocusJournalAdmission` exists to gate on purpose + consent scope + daily dose + storage cap (FocusJournalAdmission.kt:56-82). Nothing stands between `FocusSessionRuntime.emissions` (public property on a public commonMain class) and that writer, and the list accumulates identically for TUTORIAL and FAMILIARIZATION runs that the admission gate structurally denies. Mitigating today: in-memory only, never serialized (no field on `FocusRuntimeSnapshot`), the holder's `runtime` is `private`, and the emission carries no response value and no latency — the leak would be the omission pattern over trial order, not the choices. Zero blast radius today.

findings.title: The no-new-permission / no-network guard scans only commonMain, so it structurally cannot see the androidMain, iosMain and desktopMain probes where a platform API would actually appear
findings.claim: `theFocus2SourcesRequestNoPermissionAndOpenNoSocket` walks two commonMain directories only. Four of its six forbidden tokens (`SensorManager`, `LocationManager`, `java.net.`, `HttpURLConnection`) cannot compile in commonMain at all, so the assertion is close to vacuous, while the files that DO touch platform APIs — the Choreographer/CADisplayLink probes and the accessibility readers — live in source sets the walk never visits.
findings.evidence: The scan roots: `val focus2 = locate("shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/mindos/app/features/mindboost/focus2")` and `val timing = locate("shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/mindos/app/features/mindboost/core/timing")`, then `(focus2.walkTopDown() + timing.walkTopDown())` (Focus2PlatformPermissionTest.kt:31-33), checked against `FORBIDDEN_APIS = listOf("requestPermission", "android.permission", "SensorManager", "LocationManager", "java.net.", "HttpURLConnection")` (:65-72) — with the message "focus2 / core.timing must request nothing from the platform" (:42). Unscanned platform sources that exist today: `shared/src/androidMain/.../core/timing/WindowedTemporalProbe.android.kt` (which imports `android.view.Choreographer` and reads `view.display?.refreshRate`, WindowedTemporalProbe.android.kt:3 and :129), `FrameTimingProbe.android.kt`, both iosMain probes, both desktopMain probes (JVM — where `java.net.`/`HttpURLConnection` WOULD compile), and `shared/src/androidMain/.../focus2/presentation/a11y/FocusAccessibility.android.kt`, which is the one file that already queries a privileged-ish platform service (`manager.getEnabledAccessibilityServiceList(...)`, FocusAccessibility.android.kt:42-43). I verified by inspection that none of those files currently contains a forbidden token, so the claimed property HOLDS today — the defect is that the control cannot detect its violation, not that it is being violated. The sibling assertion pinning the AndroidManifest permission set (:22-27) is sound and unaffected.
findings.when_wired: A future slice adding a sensor read, a network egress or a runtime-permission request to any focus2/timing platform actual passes this gate green, and REDTEAM #31's stated purpose — "A permission appearing in a diff that also touches focus2 now turns this red and has to be justified in review" (:15-17) — is not met for the diff shape most likely to do it. Zero blast radius today (property currently holds by inspection).

findings.title: Account deletion blanket-clears mindboost_focus2, destroying another local account's REVOKED consent tombstone even though every focus2 key is already subject-prefixed
findings.claim: Every key in `mindboost_focus2` is subject-prefixed by a mandatory parameter — the same property that earned `Sessions` and `SessionRuns` their subject-scoped erasure exemption — yet focus2 is left in the blanket `clearNamespace()` loop. On a device with two local accounts, deleting account A wipes account B's `focus2_consent:B:TRIAL_JOURNAL` record, including a REVOKED one, which is precisely the fact `SecureFocusConsentStore` is architected never to lose.
findings.evidence: The blanket clear: `accountBoundStores.filterNot { store -> store === subjectScopedRunsStore || store === subjectScopedSessionsStore }.forEach { store -> store.clearNamespace() }` (AccountDeletionCoordinator.kt:67-69) — focus2 is not one of the two exclusions. focus2 keys are subject-prefixed exactly like the exempted stores: `fun prefix(userId: String) { require(ID_REGEX.matches(userId)) ...; return "focus2_session:$userId:" }` (SecureFocusSessionStore.kt:149-152) and `return "focus2_consent:$userId:${scope.name}"` (FocusDataConsent.kt:239-242). The guarantee the wipe breaks is stated explicitly: "Revocation REWRITES the record rather than deleting it: a deleted record is indistinguishable from one that was never asked, and 'the user said no' is exactly the fact we must not lose" — the class even avoids the shared read helper because quarantine deletes (FocusDataConsent.kt:140-145), and the status mapping confirms a deleted record degrades to re-askable: `this == null -> FocusConsentStatus.UNKNOWN` (:114) versus `FocusConsentStatus.REVOKED` (:115-116), where UNKNOWN is documented as "re-asking is appropriate" (:43-44).
findings.when_wired: User B, who explicitly refused per-trial journaling, is re-prompted for that consent after user A deletes their account on the shared device — the badgering the four-value status enum exists to prevent — and B's in-flight session buffer is destroyed as collateral. This is the documented legacy multi-account decision in the eraser's KDoc (AccountDeletionCoordinator.kt:26-38), so it is a known accepted class; I flag it because focus2 already satisfies the technical precondition (mandatory subject prefix) that qualified the other two namespaces for the exemption, and because the collateral here is a consent tombstone rather than regenerable data. Zero blast radius today (namespace empty, no multi-account UI).

findings.title: An unreliable assistive-technology inference is SEALED verbatim into the persisted descriptor: any enabled accessibility service is recorded as switch access
findings.claim: `switchAccessActive` is inferred from "any enabled accessibility service that is not touch exploration", and both it and `screenReaderActive` are then written to disk verbatim as fields of the sealed descriptor. The persisted record therefore asserts a disability-adjacent fact about the user that the code itself documents as wrong in both directions, and stores it as a raw signal rather than as the derived gate the engine actually consumes.
findings.evidence: The heuristic: `val otherServiceRunning = manager.isEnabled && manager.getEnabledAccessibilityServiceList(AccessibilityServiceInfo.FEEDBACK_ALL_MASK).isNotEmpty()` then `AccessibilityContext(screenReaderActive = screenReader, switchAccessActive = otherServiceRunning && !screenReader)` (FocusAccessibility.android.kt:42-47), with the accuracy limit stated in its own KDoc — "Switch access is a HEURISTIC ... It is wrong in both directions: a false positive (an autofill service, a screen filter) relabels an honest touch session" (:21-25). Both facts are then persisted: `val screenReaderActive: Boolean` is a first-class serialized field (FocusSessionDescriptor.kt:62, written at `screenReaderActive = screenReaderActive`, :204) and the inference reaches disk as `inputModalityName` via `inputModality = accessibility.impliedModality` (FocusRunPlanner.kt:93-94) → `switchAccessActive -> InputModality.SWITCH_SEQUENTIAL` (FocusSessionDescriptor.kt:275). The engine's only consumer of the pair is a derived boolean that loses nothing it needs: `val rtEvidenceAdmissible: Boolean get() = !screenReaderActive && inputModality == InputModality.TOUCH_DIRECT` (:150-151). Credit where due: the Android reader retains no service NAMES — only `.isNotEmpty()` — and the record is encrypted at rest, local-only and purged on `complete()`.
findings.when_wired: The descriptor is the only carrier of this flag today and it is purged when the run ends, so exposure is session-scoped. The risk is forward: the moment a durable history or summary sink is added, an assistive-technology flag — one that is knowingly inaccurate for anyone running a screen filter or similar service — is copied into a long-lived record unless that sink explicitly drops it, and `rtEvidenceAdmissible` shows the gate can be carried without it. Worth an explicit minimisation decision before the sink exists rather than after. Zero blast radius today (unmounted; and note `FocusRunPlanner.prepare` currently seals no temporal capability fields at all, so the coarse device-capability quartet is empty in every record).

findings.title: NO_OBSERVATION counts as a good window: a session that classified nothing returns Verdict.Eligible (absence fabricates the maximum)
findings.claim: `evaluate` treats every non-EXCLUDED bucket as evidence of good temporal capture. `windowsClassified` sums ALL buckets — including NO_OBSERVATION — and `excludedResolved` subtracts only the EXCLUDED bucket, so a window the policy explicitly refused to classify is counted both as covered and as not-excluded. A session in which EVERY window was unobservable therefore yields sessionClass=T1, coverageComplete=true, excludedFraction=0.0, causes=∅ ⇒ `Verdict.Eligible`, and `rtShadowAdmissible` then returns true. This is the exact inversion the file's own KDoc (lines 17-20) claims to close: 'reading that as "0 bad windows" would fabricate a maximum'. The existing `NotCaptured` guard cannot catch it, because it fires only on `cells.isEmpty()` (line 63) and a NoObservation window produces a NON-empty cell — the reducer folds it with its outcome (FocusSessionReducer.kt:197-199, pinned by FocusTemporalRuntimeTest.kt:93). 'We have no cells' and 'we have cells but classified nothing' are structurally different, and only the first is guarded. Worse, `windowsClassified` is a name asserting a property the arithmetic does not have, and `coverageComplete` becomes trivially true whenever every trial received ANY verdict.
findings.evidence:
FocusTemporalEligibility.kt:78 `val windowsClassified = cells.sumOf { it.cell.totalTrials }` — `cells` is `snapshot.temporalCells`, every bucket. :79-81 `val excludedResolved = cells.filter { it.bucket == TemporalWindowBucket.EXCLUDED }.sumOf { it.cell.totalTrials }` — NO_OBSERVATION is never subtracted. :92 `val coverageComplete = windowsClassified == snapshot.resolvedTrials`. :96 `if ((excludedFraction ?: FULLY_EXCLUDED) > thresholds.sessionExcludedMax)`. :105 `rtShadowVerdict = if (causes.isEmpty()) Verdict.Eligible else Verdict.Excluded(causes)`.
Reachability, three independent routes, all of which the design itself names as the interesting cases: (a) iOS ALWAYS — WindowedTemporalProbe.ios.kt:88 `expectedCadenceHz = null`, so TemporalClassPolicy.kt:50-54 returns `NoObservation` for every window; (b) Android with a detached view — WindowedTemporalProbe.android.kt:129 returns null, same path; (c) cadence mismatch (half-rate pacing), TemporalClassPolicy.kt:71-80 `cadenceResolved` false — the very scenario TemporalClassPolicy.kt:64-69 describes as the one where 'a genuinely degraded session reads flawless (the worse error, absence fabricating perfection)'. Also reached by `bufferOverflow` (TemporalWindowObservation.kt:31) and by `sampledFrames < minFramesWindow`, so the instrument's own incompleteness is laundered into eligibility — directly contradicting FrameTimeRing.kt:18-20 ('never to CLEAN (absence must never fabricate perfection)'), which is true at the policy level and reversed at the eligibility level.
ZERO test coverage of this path: FocusTemporalEligibilityAdversarialOracleTest.kt:51-52 defines the entire generated domain as `private val excluded = TemporalWindowVerdict.Excluded(TRUNCATION_RISK)` / `private val clean = TemporalWindowVerdict.Clean`; FocusTemporalEligibilityTest.kt uses only Clean/Excluded/null. A tree-wide grep for `NoObservation` finds it reaching `evaluate` in no test at all — its only focus2 test appearance is FocusTemporalRuntimeTest.kt:93, a reducer-tallying test. The 8-row truth table and the monotonicity chains are therefore all computed over a domain that omits the failing value.
findings.when_wired: Blast radius TODAY is zero — focus2 has no production call-site (verified: 0 consumers). WHEN WIRED (Paso 4 wires this candidate, per the file's own line 15), an iOS session admits its RTs to the shadow ledger having produced no temporal evidence whatsoever, and an Android session pacing at half the panel rate does the same. The shadow lane is the foundation the future official RT lane is calibrated on, so a shadow ledger silently populated from unobserved sessions poisons the calibration rather than one verdict. Fix direction: NO_OBSERVATION must be its own cause (either COVERAGE_INCOMPLETE counted against it, or a fourth ExclusionCause), never folded in with CLEAN — and the oracle's verdict domain must be widened to all four TemporalWindowVerdict values before this is re-declared green.

findings.title: The mounted sibling probe still fabricates the nominal cadence, and the Paso-7 honesty guard is scoped by filename so it cannot see it
findings.claim: Paso 7 removed `?: DEFAULT_REFRESH_HZ` from `WindowedTemporalProbe.android.kt` and wrote a guard whose KDoc states the rule universally — 'no adapter may substitute a nominal cadence for an absent one'. `FrameTimingProbe.android.kt`, member #1 of this same manifest, in the same package and directory, still performs exactly that substitution, twice on consecutive lines, and its KDoc advertises it as a feature. The guard pins its scope with two hardcoded file-path constants and never scans this third adapter, so the universal rule is enforced on the two files that already comply. This repeats the guard-scoping failure the guard's own KDoc (lines 34-39) says a first draft made: the previous draft's slice was too narrow within one file; this one's is too narrow across files.
findings.evidence:
FrameTimingProbe.android.kt:55-56 `val hz = view.display?.refreshRate?.toDouble() ?: FrameStatsCalculator.DEFAULT_REFRESH_HZ` / `if (hz > 0.0) hz else FrameStatsCalculator.DEFAULT_REFRESH_HZ`, documented at :47-48 as 'Falls back to the conservative 60 Hz nominal when the view is not yet attached or the platform reports a non-positive rate.'
The sibling declares the same act forbidden: WindowedTemporalProbe.android.kt:28-33 'Substituting a nominal 60 Hz here would make an ABSENT platform statement classify... the two adapters must fail the same way or the platforms are not comparable' and :126-127 'No fallback constant'.
The guard's scope: WindowedTemporalProbeCadenceHonestyTest.kt:10 '**no adapter may substitute a nominal cadence for an absent one**' vs :95-100 `const val ANDROID_ADAPTER = "...WindowedTemporalProbe.android.kt"` / `const val IOS_ADAPTER = "...WindowedTemporalProbe.ios.kt"` — FrameTimingProbe.android.kt is not among them.
The fabrication is self-refuting inside its own file: :13-16 'On a 90/120 Hz panel a 60 Hz-hardcoded nominal made real jank a false negative — frames pacing at the 60 Hz period (16.67 ms) looked smooth against a 16.67 ms nominal instead of dropped against the true 8.33 ms one.' The hardcode was removed; the fallback that reproduces it whenever `View.getDisplay()` returns null was not. The provider is invoked at :41 inside `stop()`, i.e. at segment teardown — precisely when detachment is plausible.
findings.when_wired: THIS ONE IS ALREADY WIRED — the only finding here with non-zero blast radius today. `SpeedExerciseScreen.kt:112 val frameProbe = rememberFrameTimingProbe()` → `:142 frameProbe = frameProbe` → `SpeedSessionStateHolder.kt:325 val frameStats = frameProbe.stop()` → `:333-334 frameDropFraction = frameStats.frameDropFraction, criticalFrameJitter = frameStats.criticalFrameJitter` into `QualitySignals` → `qualityEvaluator.evaluate`. On a 90/120 Hz device with a detached view at stop time, real drops are measured against a 16.67 ms nominal, read as smooth, and the Speed session's quality decision is derived from a constant nobody measured — understating jank, which admits a degraded session to the profile. Fix: make the provider `() -> Double?` like its sibling and let absence propagate, and rescope the guard to the directory (or to any file naming the constant outside a declared exception) rather than to two filenames.

findings.title: The destructive probe drain still precedes the rejection check — the ordering the Paso-7 removal comment identifies as the root cause it was fixing
findings.claim: `submit` drains the probe before `runtime.respond(...)` can reject the input. `drainWindow()` is a MUTATION, not a read: it empties the ring's interval and (on Android) clears the pending render marker. So an out-of-phase `submit` — a response arriving when no window is open — consumes and discards the currently-open window's frames and its marker, and returns having folded nothing. The next window's observation is short by that whole interval. The removal comment 130 lines above diagnoses exactly this ordering as the defect it was removing ('it appended BEFORE the runtime's rejection check, so an out-of-phase tap... added a phantom entry'), removed the symptom (the list), and left the ordering.
findings.evidence:
FocusTracerStateHolder.kt:204-212: `suspend fun submit(response: Response, atElapsedNanos: Long = clock.elapsedNanos()) {` / `:205 val observation = probe.drainWindow()` / `:206-208 val verdict = observation?.let { TemporalClassPolicy.windowIntegrity(it, temporalThresholds) }` / `:210 if (runtime.respond(response, atElapsedNanos, verdict, sampled).wasRejected) return`.
The rejection is real and reachable: FocusSessionRuntime.kt:106-109 `val facts = currentTrial ?: return FocusReduction(snapshot, rejection = FocusRejection.TrialInputOutOfPhase(...))`, plus FocusSessionReducer.kt:161-165 (`!snapshot.hasOpenWindow || presentedAt == null || deadline == null`).
The drain is destructive: FrameTimeRing.kt:57-67 `drain()` sets `size = 0; writeIndex = 0; overflowed = false` and retains only the last frame as anchor; WindowedTemporalProbe.android.kt:72-73 `val marker = markerDelayNanos; markerDelayNanos = null`.
The self-diagnosis: FocusTracerStateHolder.kt:75-83 'REMOVED in Paso 7 (exit gate): `windowVerdicts`... Worse for a measurement device, it appended BEFORE the runtime's rejection check, so an out-of-phase tap (a double tap after the trial had already resolved) added a phantom entry that matched no resolved window'.
findings.when_wired: Blast radius today is zero (unmounted; `submit` is currently reached only from `runSession`'s once-per-trial loop). WHEN WIRED, any second entry point into `submit` — an accessibility action, a double-dispatch, a UI that calls it directly rather than through `onResponse` — silently strips frames from the live window. It composes badly with the first finding: a window robbed of its frames falls below `minFramesWindow` (TemporalClassPolicy.kt:52) and becomes NoObservation, which per F1 is then counted as a GOOD window. An out-of-phase tap would thus convert a real window into a fabricated-clean one. Fix: dispatch to the runtime first and drain only on a non-rejected reduction, or make the drain non-destructive until the input is accepted.

findings.title: iOS class KDoc still documents the self-detect-and-classify design the same file repudiates 55 lines later
findings.claim: The class KDoc presents self-detection of the refresh rate as the adapter's deliberate, correct design, with a rationale (avoiding the ProMotion false positive). The inline comment inside `drainWindow` names that same design as the defect Paso 5 removed, with the opposite rationale (it produces the false NEGATIVE the charter forbids). Both paragraphs are in the working tree, in the same file, describing the same decision in contradictory terms. A reader arriving at the class doc — the first thing read — is told the adapter classifies against a self-detected rate, which is no longer what it does (`expectedCadenceHz = null` means it classifies nothing).
findings.evidence:
WindowedTemporalProbe.ios.kt:26-29 'The per-drain refresh rate is SELF-DETECTED from the median frame delta (C.1: real Hz, never the panel maximum) — on a ProMotion panel pacing at 60 Hz, classifying against the 120 Hz maximum would read normal pacing as drops and exclude honest sessions (a false negative the charter forbids).'
vs :83-88 'NO expected cadence on iOS in S5 (Paso 5, B4)... Self-detecting the rate and classifying against it — what this adapter used to do implicitly — makes a half-rate window read as flawless, which is the false negative the charter forbids. Declared absent ⇒ NotCaptured.'
The two also disagree on which error is the false negative. Note the iOS use of the nominal constant at :76 `FrameStatsCalculator.fromFrameTimes(times, detectedHz ?: FrameStatsCalculator.DEFAULT_REFRESH_HZ)` is DECLARED and deliberate (blessed by WindowedTemporalProbeCadenceHonestyTest.kt:52-56), so it is not itself a defect — but the stale class doc is what makes it read as one.
findings.when_wired: No runtime effect in any state — documentation only. The risk is a future maintainer trusting the class doc, concluding the adapter already classifies honestly against a detected rate, and 'restoring' `expectedCadenceHz = detectedHz` — which is precisely the change the inline comment exists to prevent and which would re-open the half-rate-reads-flawless inversion. Blast radius today: zero.

findings.title: The ±5% cadence tolerance exists as two private constants in two files, tied together only by a sentence of KDoc
findings.claim: `CADENCE_MATCH_TOLERANCE` documents itself as being the same width as `HzBand`'s band tolerance and asserts that equality as a fact about another file's private constant. Nothing enforces it. The thresholds constant is pinned against the protocol doc by a parity test; the HzBand constant is pinned by nothing that relates the two. Changing either leaves the other's KDoc silently false. This is the 'keep in sync' comment pattern the parity machinery elsewhere in this very diff exists to replace: TemporalQualityThresholdsParityTest was built precisely because a documented number and a code number can diverge without failing a build.
findings.evidence:
TemporalQualityThresholds.kt:94-95 `/** ±5%, the same width [HzBand] uses to call two rates the same panel cadence. */` / `private const val CADENCE_MATCH_TOLERANCE: Double = 0.05` — private, consumed at TemporalClassPolicy.kt:79 `abs(detected - expected) <= expected * thresholds.cadenceMatchTolerance`.
HzBand.kt:24-25 `/** Bands match within ±5% of the standard rate (119.4 and 120.6 both land in [HZ_120]). */` / `private const val BAND_TOLERANCE_FRACTION: Double = 0.05` — private, consumed only at HzBand.kt:29.
The parity test covers the thresholds side against the doc (TemporalQualityThresholdsParityTest.kt:58 `"cadenceMatchTolerance" to code.cadenceMatchTolerance`) and never touches HzBand. Note the file's own rule at TemporalQualityThresholds.kt:9-10: 'Role separation (never reuse a constant across roles)' — which is a good reason for two constants, but then the KDoc should not assert their equality as a standing fact.
findings.when_wired: No runtime effect while both remain 0.05. If HzBand's banding tolerance is ever widened (a new panel family, a detection-noise fix), the classification tolerance silently stops matching the doc's claim, and a reader reasoning from the KDoc will believe two rates that band together also resolve together. Either pin the equality with a test, or delete the cross-reference and let each constant stand on its own role. Blast radius today: zero.

findings.title: Android and iOS write the same droppedFrames field from different referents and different roundings; iOS systematically under-counts
findings.claim: Two divergences in one field. (a) Android derives droppedFrames/criticalFrameJitter against the PLATFORM-STATED cadence; iOS derives them against a median taken from the very trace being classified — self-consistent by construction, so a half-rate stream yields zero drops. (b) The same derived quantity is rounded two different ways: roundToInt() on Android, toInt() on iOS. Truncation loses a drop whenever the float lands just under the integer, and it always errs toward FEWER drops — the understating-jank direction. This is not theoretical: for sampledFrames=22 with 15 real drops, (15/22)*22 = 14.999999999999998, so Android reports 15 and iOS reports 14; 76,617 such (n,d) pairs exist for n<=2000.

findings.title: The session backstop has no minimum denominator, and non-capture scores better than partial capture that caught a bad window
findings.claim: The only route by which the temporal axis demotes accuracy evidence is a ratio with no sample floor, so one classified window can decide a 100-trial session. The resulting ordering is perverse: a session that classified nothing (empty cells ⇒ null fraction ⇒ NO_BACKSTOP 0.0) stays PROVISIONAL, while the SAME session that managed to classify one window and found it excluded (fraction 1/1 = 1.0) is demoted to TRAINING_ONLY. Capturing slightly more evidence is punished harder than capturing none, which is the incentive gradient a measurement engine least wants.
findings.evidence: FocusEvidenceStatePolicy.kt:45 `(temporal?.excludedFraction ?: NO_BACKSTOP) > thresholds.sessionExcludedMax ->` — the only temporal demotion path, and the only guard on the ratio's provenance. The ratio itself: FocusTemporalEligibility.kt:89-91 `val denominator = windowsClassified + discards` / `if (denominator > 0) (excludedResolved + discards).toDouble() / denominator else null` — no minimum-n check anywhere, in contrast with the frame-count floors that DO exist for the classes (TemporalQualityThresholds.kt:24-26 `minFramesWindow` / `minFramesSession`). The asymmetry is directly demonstrable from the two existing tests: FocusTemporalEligibilityTest.kt:58-67 (empty cells ⇒ fraction null) versus :133-146 (one discard over one classified ⇒ 0.5), extended to 1/1 ⇒ 1.0 > 0.50.
findings.when_wired: A partially-instrumented session (probe starting late, buffer overflowing on most windows) can lose its provisional accuracy evidence on the strength of a single classified window, while a fully un-instrumented session keeps it. Blast radius today zero (unmounted).
