findings.title: The 0/0 trap is pinned only for EMPTY cells; a session of all-NoObservation windows evaluates Eligible with excludedFraction 0.0, and no test covers it
findings.claim: The test section header reads "--- The 0/0 trap: absence is NotCaptured, never Eligible ('0 bad') nor Excluded ('0 good') ---" and `emptyCells_isNotCaptured_neverEligibleNorExcluded` is the only test of it. It exercises ONE kind of absence: `sessionWith(verdicts = listOf(null, null))`, i.e. no probe wired, cells empty. The other kind — the probe ran, drained, and the policy honestly refused to classify — is never evaluated. Grep confirms only three files construct `TemporalWindowVerdict.NoObservation` (TemporalClassPolicyTest, NoOpWindowedTemporalProbeTest, FocusTemporalRuntimeTest.kt:93) and NONE of them calls `FocusTemporalEligibility.evaluate`.
findings.evidence: FocusTemporalEligibility.kt:78 `val windowsClassified = cells.sumOf { it.cell.totalTrials }` counts EVERY bucket, NO_OBSERVATION included; :79-81 `cells.filter { it.bucket == TemporalWindowBucket.EXCLUDED }` so unclassified windows contribute 0 to the numerator; :91 `if (denominator > 0) (excludedResolved + discards).toDouble() / denominator else null` → 0.0; :92 `coverageComplete = windowsClassified == snapshot.resolvedTrials` → true. FocusSessionReducer.kt:197 folds ANY non-null verdict (`temporalVerdict?.let { snapshot.temporalTallying(...) }`), and TemporalWindowVerdict.kt:54 maps `NoObservation -> TemporalWindowBucket.NO_OBSERVATION`, so the cells are non-empty and the NotCaptured short-circuit at FocusTemporalEligibility.kt:63 (`probeCapability == null || cells.isEmpty()`) never fires. Frames still accumulate: FocusTracerStateHolder.kt:209 `val sampled = observation?.sampledFrames ?: 0` is added regardless of classifiability, so `sessionClass` reaches T1 (ProbeCapability.IOS_CADISPLAYLINK.expectedDomain == ClockDomain.IOS_CADISPLAYLINK_MACH_TIME, TemporalVocabulary.kt:48). Result: causes empty ⇒ `Verdict.Eligible`. iOS reaches this on EVERY session — WindowedTemporalProbe.ios.kt:88 `expectedCadenceHz = null` ⇒ TemporalClassPolicy.kt:53 `!cadenceResolved(...)` ⇒ NoObservation for every window. No mutation is needed to make this green: it is green now.
findings.when_wired: The RT shadow lane admits a session in which not one window was temporally classifiable, and `FocusEvidenceStatePolicy.rtShadowAdmissible` returns true for it (given NANOS_NATIVE + touch modality). Every iOS session would enter the shadow ledger labelled Eligible with 'zero exclusion'. Blast radius today is ZERO (engine unmounted, zero production call-sites). The fix is a policy decision, not a test: either NO_OBSERVATION windows must be excluded from `windowsClassified`/`coverageComplete`, or a fourth cause must fire when the classified-and-resolved fraction is 0 — and then a test that drives an all-NoObservation session through `evaluate()`.

findings.title: The a11y answer-leak test only exercises a pure string helper; the composed semantics tree (where each arrow is its own node) is untested and the Row does not merge
findings.claim: The test KDoc says "The discriminating check is INVARIANCE, not a substring blocklist (which a paraphrase could dodge)" and FocusTracerScreen.kt:152 says "FocusTracerA11yLeakTest pins the invariance". Both tests call `stimulusContentDescription(trial)` directly — a pure function whose body (FocusTracerScreen.kt:154-158) mentions neither `centrePointsLeft` nor `congruent`, so the invariance it asserts is true BY CONSTRUCTION of that function and cannot fail while the function keeps ignoring both fields. What is never tested is the thing a screen reader actually traverses: the composed semantics tree.
findings.evidence: FocusTracerScreen.kt:132-140 — `Row(... modifier = Modifier.semantics { contentDescription = description }) { repeat(perSide) { Text(flanker, ...) }; Text(centre, ...); repeat(...) { Text(flanker, ...) } }`. `Modifier.semantics { }` is NON-merging (no `mergeDescendants = true`, no `clearAndSetSemantics`), so each child `Text("◀"/"▶")` remains its own semantics node carrying its glyph as `text`. The KDoc two lines above (FocusTracerScreen.kt:121) asserts the opposite: "The whole row carries ONE description rather than one per arrow." `centre` (line 127) is the correct response and `flanker` (line 128) encodes congruency, so per-node traversal reconstructs both. The repo's own 2026-07-01 learning already records that Compose ContentDescription semantics on a parent ACCUMULATE with descendants rather than replace them.
findings.when_wired: A screen-reader participant could recover direction and congruency by traversing the individual glyph nodes, voiding the flanker conflict. Accuracy is NOT protected by the modality gate: FocusSessionDescriptor.kt:151 `rtEvidenceAdmissible get() = !screenReaderActive && inputModality == TOUCH_DIRECT` gates only RT, and FocusEvidenceStatePolicy.kt:30-32 explicitly declares modality "never demotes the SESSION (accuracy is modality-fair)" — so a leaked-answer session still yields PROVISIONAL accuracy evidence. Zero blast radius today. A test asserting the merged semantics tree (or `mergeDescendants = true` / `clearAndSetSemantics`) is what would actually pin the claim.

findings.title: "Official tallies are IDENTICAL with and without a temporal verdict" is pinned only at trial-COUNT granularity, never at SDT composition

findings.title: The permission/no-network guard scans only commonMain, where every forbidden API is structurally unreachable; androidMain and iosMain are never scanned

findings.title: "Changing any threshold requires a new version" is enforced by nothing; the classifying numbers are pinned only within wide bands, and the doc↔code parity moves with the code
